name: v0.13.1
body:
Fathom 0.13.1 adds Interface Size on desktop, saves Android YouTube downloads where other apps can find them, includes ffmpeg on Windows, and fixes Quick Connect on Jellyfin 12 and the Android media controls.

## Added
- Interface Size (Linux and Windows), in Settings > Appearance: make everything bigger or smaller, from 75% to 200%. Automatic follows your display, and on Linux it also sizes up on a dense screen, such as a 4K monitor, when the desktop's scaling is left at 100%.
- Settings > Support: Ko-fi, GitHub Sponsors, and free ways to help.

## Changed
- The Windows build includes ffmpeg, so YouTube downloads above 360p work with nothing else to install, including the growing number of videos YouTube only offers as separate video and audio. The download is about 38 MB larger.
- Changing a download folder offers to move the downloads already in the old one, and asks only when there are some.
- Jellyfin downloads are saved under readable names with their real file extension, such as `Bullet Train (2022).mkv` or `Show - S01E02 - Episode.mp4`, so other apps and file managers recognize them. Downloads you already have keep their names.
- Diagnostics on Android include presses from the notification, lock screen, and headset buttons, and changes in audio focus.

## Fixed
- Quick Connect failed with "The server returned an error (405)" on Jellyfin 12. (#53, thanks @mmtechslv)
- On Android, notification, lock screen, and earbud controls could stop responding after you stopped playback and started it again, or after listening in another app. Disconnecting your earbuds pauses Fathom again, and two apps no longer play over each other.
- On Android, YouTube downloads were saved where only Fathom could see them. They now go to Movies/Fathom and Music/Fathom, or the folder you pick, and existing ones move there once. A download's menu offers Open With and Share in place of Show in Folder.
- On Android, Download & Install could fail with "Download failed" after you left Fathom and came back. The Updates screen now shows why an update failed.
- On Android, backing out of the installer meant downloading the whole update again. A downloaded update is now reused, and the button says Install.
- Radio retries within seconds after a dropped connection, including with the screen off, instead of waiting up to a minute. Pausing while it reconnects stops the retries.
- Without ffmpeg, the download sheet offered a 360p file for videos YouTube no longer offers one for.
- On Android TV, the Movie Night Wheel's focus ring was a square box instead of a circle.

## Security
- There are no open security advisories against Fathom's dependencies. The ffmpeg included on Windows is the current release (9.0.2), and a weekly check keeps it current.

## Install
- Linux: `Fathom-x86_64.AppImage` (or `Fathom-aarch64.AppImage`), `chmod +x` and run.
- Windows: `Fathom-Setup-x64.exe` to install, or `Fathom-windows-x64.zip` to unzip and run `fathom.exe`.
- Android (phones, tablets, and experimental Android TV): `Fathom-0.13.1.apk`.

Fathom is free and always will be. Support on [Ko-fi](https://ko-fi.com/traceapps) goes toward a Mac and an iPhone so my apps can come to Apple devices, and [GitHub Sponsors](https://github.com/sponsors/TraceApps?metadata_app=fathom&metadata_from=release) helps with the monthly costs.

name: v0.13.1-dev04
body:
Fourth dev pre-release of the 0.13.1 patch.

### Added
- **Settings, Support:** a new page with Ko-fi, GitHub Sponsors and free ways to help.

### Changed
- **Downloads** from your Jellyfin server are saved under readable names with their real file extension, such as `Bullet Train (2022).mkv` or `Show - S01E02 - Episode.mp4`, so other apps and file managers recognise them. Downloads you already have keep their current names.
- **Diagnostics** now include the media commands Android delivers to Fathom (from the notification, lock screen, earbuds and headsets) and changes in audio focus, to pin down controls that stop responding.

### Fixed
- **Android:** notification, lock screen and earbud controls could stop responding after you stopped playback in Fathom and started it again. Fathom now stays connected to them.
- **Android:** after another app has played audio, pressing play in Fathom takes the audio back, so disconnecting your earbuds pauses it again and two apps no longer play over each other.

Tester build, report anything odd. New this round especially: media controls after stopping and restarting playback, or after listening in another app; and the names of new downloads. If the controls stop responding, copy the Diagnostics report: its new Android media commands section shows where each press went. The in-app updater's Dev channel will offer this build automatically.

Fathom is free and always will be. Support on [Ko-fi](https://ko-fi.com/traceapps) goes toward a Mac and an iPhone so my apps can come to Apple devices, and [GitHub Sponsors](https://github.com/sponsors/TraceApps?metadata_app=fathom&metadata_from=release) helps with the monthly costs.

Tester build, report anything odd. New this round especially: radio after a connection drop (try airplane mode for a few seconds, screen on and off), and reopening the update screen after backing out of the installer. The in-app updater's Dev channel will offer this build automatically.

name: v0.13.1-dev01
body:
First dev pre-release of the 0.13.1 patch.

### Changed
- **Windows:** ffmpeg now comes with Fathom, so YouTube downloads above 360p work with nothing else to install. That includes the growing number of videos YouTube only offers as separate video and audio. The download is about 38 MB larger.
- **Android:** YouTube downloads are saved to Movies/Fathom (video) and Music/Fathom (audio), or to the folder you pick, so they show up in the Files app, your gallery and other players. Downloads you already have are moved there the first time you open this version.

### Fixed
- **Android:** Download & Install could fail with "Download failed" after you left Fathom and came back while music or a video was paused. The update downloaded fine, but the system installer never opened. If an update fails on a build older than this one, force stop Fathom, reopen it, and try again.
- The Updates screen now shows the reason when an update fails.
- **Android:** YouTube downloads were saved to a folder only Fathom could see, and Show in Folder did nothing.
- Without ffmpeg, the download sheet no longer promises a 360p file for videos YouTube doesn't offer one for, and the error explains why.
- **Android TV:** the Movie Night Wheel's focus ring is now round, matching the wheel, instead of a square box.

Tester build, report anything odd. New this round especially: YouTube downloads on Android and Windows, and in-app updates after reopening the app. The in-app updater's Dev channel will offer this build automatically.

Fathom is free and always will be. The [Mac fund](https://ko-fi.com/traceapps) is for a Mac, so Fathom can come to macOS and iOS.

name: v0.13.0
body:
Fathom 0.13.0 adds a Watchlist, the Movie Night Wheel, a sleep timer, multi-select, and online subtitle search; shows every kind of subtitle; gets ready for Jellyfin 12; and brings server backups and the full user editor to the admin screens.

## Added
- Watchlist: a "want to watch" list, separate from Favorites. Toggle it from a detail page's bookmark icon or any item's menu, find it from the Libraries browse bar, or add it to the main navigation under Settings > Navigation. It syncs across your devices through your Jellyfin account.
- Movie Night Wheel: spin to settle what to watch, from the Watchlist or a SyncPlay session so a group can decide together. Fill it from your library or type titles in, and pick a mode: Last One Standing, Single Spin, or Best of 3.
- Sleep Timer on every player (video, music, YouTube, and radio): 15 minutes to 2 hours, or the end of the current track or episode, with the sound fading out over the last 15 seconds.
- Multi-select in library grids: choose Select from any poster's menu, then mark watched or unwatched, favorite, add to a playlist, or delete (with the right permission) all at once. YouTube downloads can be selected and deleted in bulk too.
- Remove from Continue Watching, from a card's menu. It takes the show or film off the row until you watch it again, and clears its resume point on the server so Jellyfin's other apps agree.
- Extras on detail pages: trailers, behind the scenes, deleted scenes, interviews, and other bonus material stored with a title get their own row.
- Search Subtitles Online, at the bottom of the subtitle menu: finds subtitles through the provider installed on your Jellyfin server (such as the OpenSubtitles plugin) and adds the one you pick straight to the video, with matches for your exact file listed first.
- Volume Levelling for music (Settings > Audio): Per Track or Per Album, using the ReplayGain levels in your files.
- YouTube chapters shown the way YouTube shows them: the current chapter in a pill beside the volume control, a seek bar split at each chapter, and the chapter named as you scrub.
- Foldable phones: half-fold the phone with the crease across the screen and the video takes the standing half, with the controls (or, on YouTube, the details and comments) on the flat half.
- Radio next and previous station controls, on the Now Playing screen, the Android notification, Android Auto, and the Linux and Windows media controls. (#41, thanks @Epic-dog)
- Server administration:
  - Backups: create a backup of the server (database, plus optional metadata, subtitles, and trickplay), see what each one holds, and restore one.
  - The user editor now covers everything the web dashboard offers: forced transcoding of remote sources, SyncPlay access, deletion limited to chosen libraries, device and channel allow-lists, allowed and blocked tags, access schedules, blocking unrated items by type, and sign-in providers where the server has more than one.
- A Windows installer, with a Start menu entry and an uninstaller, alongside the portable zip. (#43, thanks @Epic-dog)
- A Download Location setting (General > Storage) for downloaded Jellyfin media, organized into Movies, TV Shows, Music, and Recordings folders.
- YouTube downloads on Android now use a full ffmpeg, as on desktop: video above 360p, MKV, and MP3 all work. (#46, thanks @urtaevS)
- A floating progress pill for YouTube downloads, matching the one for Jellyfin downloads.
- Screen reader support: posters are announced as one item with their title and year, and every icon-only button carries a label.

## Changed
- Continue Watching follows what you actually watch: one card per show, whether you stopped part-way through an episode or finished one and the next is waiting, ordered by what you watched most recently. A new episode of a show you were caught up on goes near the front the day it arrives.
- The Home banner mixes a few things you are watching with what was added recently.
- Subtitle and audio tracks are named from what the server knows about them instead of a bare language code, for example English (Forced, SRT), English (Picture, PGS), English (External, SRT), and English (DTS-HD MA 5.1). Tracks that would otherwise look identical are numbered.
- Ready for Jellyfin 12: Fathom uses the server routes Jellyfin 12 documents, in place of older ones Jellyfin 12 dropped from its API, and saves parental ratings with Jellyfin 12's rating scores. Older servers keep working.
- Right-click, long-press, and the "..." button open the same menu everywhere, including Downloads, radio stations, album tracks, and Seerr requests: a dropdown at the pointer on desktop, a sheet on touch and TV.
- Messages, loading spinners, and confirmations look and behave the same throughout, and destructive confirmations start with Cancel focused.
- The Inter typeface is bundled with the app instead of fetched from Google Fonts on first launch.
- YouTube downloads are split into Downloading and Downloaded sections, and the download-complete notification opens them.
- "Add Favorite" now reads "Add to Favorites", matching the Watchlist.
- The keyboard Shortcuts settings no longer appear on phones and tablets.
- The Linux AppImage no longer carries AppImageUpdate data. Updating from inside Fathom works as before.

## Fixed
- Picture-based subtitles (Blu-ray PGS, DVD VobSub, DVB) never appeared when selected.
- Subtitle files stored beside the video, including ones a server plugin downloaded, were missing from the subtitle menu.
- YouTube chapters stopped appearing after YouTube moved them.
- Starting a title again straight after watching it could resume from an earlier spot, and on Android a resumed video could snap back to the beginning.
- Fathom crashed on startup on Linux setups with no system keyring at all, such as Steam Big Picture and gamescope. It now falls back to a local store. (#32, thanks @tangowithfoxtrot)
- Requesting through Seerr while signed in with a Jellyfin username and password failed with an API key error.
- The YouTube What's New tab could spin for minutes or come back empty with a large subscription list. (#38, thanks @jtbrauer92-p)
- On the Now Playing screens, the volume control covered the Play button or the repeat button, and the screen could go blank below the seek bar after the on-screen keyboard. (#40, thanks @urtaevS)
- Radio reconnects at the live edge after a dropped connection, resumes after another app briefly takes the audio (a call or a voice recorder), and its volume control no longer runs off-screen.
- Downloaded YouTube videos now play like online ones: resume, lock-screen details, Next, picture-in-picture, captions, and SponsorBlock.
- Several YouTube downloads at once no longer slow each other down.
- In server administration, choosing None for hardware acceleration or Auto for the encoder preset stopped the Transcoding page saving.
- The Home banner could show one title's details over another's backdrop.
- Marking an episode watched from Next Up didn't update its checkmark in the episode list.
- Dragging a video down the YouTube queue dropped it one slot too far.
- The desktop fullscreen title bar reappeared when an episode advanced to the next.
- Buttons overflowed in the Up Next card, the SyncPlay group list, and Seerr's request dialogs in some languages.
- Android Auto browsing showed an error after a dropped connection instead of recovering.
- The volume control's icon disappeared in the light theme.

## Security
- Every dependency is updated to its latest version. There are no open security advisories against Fathom's dependencies.

## Install
- Linux: `Fathom-x86_64.AppImage` (or `Fathom-aarch64.AppImage`), `chmod +x` and run.
- Windows: `Fathom-Setup-x64.exe` to install, or `Fathom-windows-x64.zip` to unzip and run `fathom.exe`.
- Android (phones, tablets, and experimental Android TV): `Fathom-0.13.0.apk`.

name: v0.13.0-dev05
body:
Fifth dev pre-release of the 0.13.0 minor.

### Added
- Search Subtitles Online, at the bottom of the subtitle menu: finds subtitles through the subtitle provider installed on your Jellyfin server (such as the OpenSubtitles plugin) and adds the one you pick straight to the video. Results show the release name, provider, format and download count, with anything matching your exact file listed first. Searches your preferred subtitle language, or your device's language if you haven't set one, and Change Language searches another. Shown to administrators and to accounts allowed to manage subtitles.

### Changed
- Subtitle and audio tracks are now named from what the server knows about them instead of a bare language code: for example English (Forced, SRT), English (Picture, PGS), English (External, SRT) and English (DTS-HD MA 5.1). Tracks that would otherwise look identical are numbered.
- Fathom now uses the server routes Jellyfin 12 documents. Jellyfin 12 removed a set of older routes from its API that Fathom relied on for libraries, Continue Watching, item details, favorites, watched state, profile pictures and more. They still work for now but could disappear in any update. Older servers keep working.

### Fixed
- Picture-based subtitles (Blu-ray PGS, DVD VobSub, DVB) never appeared when selected.
- Subtitles stored in their own file beside the video, including ones downloaded by a server plugin, were missing from the subtitle menu.

Tester build, report anything odd. New this round especially: subtitles (picture-based and external tracks, and online search) and the Jellyfin 12 route changes, which touch every screen. The in-app updater's Dev channel will offer this build automatically.

name: v0.13.0-dev04
body:
Fourth dev pre-release of the 0.13.0 minor.

Fixes resume, which was broken in the last two dev builds: nothing you watched saved where you stopped. Please update.

### Added
- YouTube chapters now show the way they do on YouTube: the current chapter's title sits in a pill next to the volume control and opens the chapter list when tapped, the seek bar splits into a segment per chapter, and dragging or hovering the bar names the chapter you would land in.
- Tabletop layout for the YouTube player on foldable phones: half-fold the phone with the crease across the screen and the video takes the standing half, with the title, comments and Up Next on the flat half. Fullscreen splits the same way, video above the crease and controls below.

### Fixed
- Resume was broken everywhere: Fathom never told the server that playback had started, so nothing saved where you stopped and every title played from the beginning. Anything you watched on dev02 or dev03 has no resume point, so those titles start over once more.
- On Android, a video that did resume could jump to the saved spot and then snap back to the beginning.
- Starting a title straight after watching it resumed from the previous session's spot rather than the last one.
- YouTube chapters had stopped appearing at all, including in the chapter list, after YouTube moved them.
- In the YouTube audio player, the volume button sat on top of the play button instead of at the right edge like every other player.
- Administration: editing a user (loading, permissions, password, delete) and the General, Transcoding and Networking server settings pages could not load or save.

Tester build, report anything odd. New this round especially: resume working again, and YouTube chapters. The in-app updater's Dev channel will offer this build automatically.

name: v0.13.0-dev03
body:
Third dev pre-release of the 0.13.0 minor.

### Added
- Remove from Continue Watching, from a card's menu (long-press, right-click, or the hover menu). It takes that show or film off the row until you watch it again, and clears its resume point on the server so Jellyfin's other apps agree.
- Multi-select in library grids: choose Select from any poster's menu, tap more titles or use Select All, then Mark Watched, Mark Unwatched, Add to Favorites or Add to Playlist for all of them at once. Delete is there too for accounts allowed to delete media.
- Extras on detail pages: trailers, behind the scenes, deleted scenes, interviews and other bonus features stored with a title now appear in their own row.
- Volume Levelling for music, in Preferences under Audio: Per Track or Per Album, using the ReplayGain levels in your files, so songs play at a similar loudness.
- Tabletop layout on foldable phones: half-fold the phone with the crease across the screen and the video sits in the top half with the controls on the bottom half.

### Changed
- Continue Watching now works like Netflix and Plex: one card per show, whether you stopped partway through an episode or finished one and the next is waiting, ordered by what you actually watched last. A half-watched episode you abandoned long ago gives way to where you really are in the show, and a new episode of a show you were caught up on goes near the front the day it arrives.
- The Home banner now mixes three things you're watching with three new additions, instead of only new additions.

### Fixed
- The Home banner could show one title's details over another title's backdrop after the list refreshed.
- Radio stayed paused after another app briefly took the audio, such as a voice recorder or a call. It now picks back up when the interruption ends, and keeps retrying a stream that drops instead of giving up after the first failure.
- Marking an episode watched from a show's Next Up didn't update its checkmark in the episode list until you left the page.
- On Android, the Movie Night Wheel's ticks sounded slower than on desktop and the spin stuttered. Both now match desktop.
- Dragging a video down the queue in Now Playing dropped it one slot too far.

Tester build, report anything odd. New this round especially: the new Continue Watching and Remove, multi-select, and radio recovering after an interruption. The in-app updater's Dev channel will offer this build automatically.

name: v0.13.0-dev02
body:
Second dev pre-release of the 0.13.0 minor.

### Added
- Movie Night Wheel: a spin-the-wheel way to settle what to watch, from the Watchlist screen or a SyncPlay session so a group can decide together. Fill it from your library or type titles in, then pick a mode: Last One Standing knocks a title out on every spin until one is left, Single Spin takes the first result, and Best of 3 picks the first title the wheel lands on twice. Flick it with a mouse or a finger, undo a spin that went wrong, and the winner arrives with its poster, overview and rating, plus Play, Watch Trailer and Add to Watchlist.
- Sleep Timer on every player (music, video, YouTube and radio), from the gear menu or the moon button in the top bar. Choose 15 to 120 minutes, or stop at the end of the current track or episode. Sound fades out over the last 15 seconds instead of cutting off, and the button shows the time left while it runs.
- Screen reader support: a poster card is announced as one button with its title and year rather than read out piece by piece, every icon-only button has a tooltip that doubles as its spoken label, and the wheel names itself, spins on the activate gesture, and reads out each result.

### Changed
- The Inter typeface is now bundled with the app instead of fetched from Google Fonts on first run, so there is no third-party request at startup and the right font on a first launch with no internet.
- Messages, busy spinners and confirmation dialogs now look and behave the same everywhere: one message style with consistent timing and no stacking, one spinner size and weight, and confirmations where anything destructive is red and starts with the focus on Cancel, so a stray Enter cannot delete something.

### Fixed
- On desktop, the Now Playing volume control sat on top of Pause. It now sits to the right of the transport controls and opens over the page, so nothing shifts when it opens.
- The volume control was drawn in a fixed near-black that hid its own icon in the light theme.
- Browsing in Android Auto after a dropped connection or an expired token broke the request instead of falling back to an empty folder.

Tester build, report anything odd. New this round especially: the Movie Night Wheel and the Sleep Timer. The in-app updater's Dev channel will offer this build automatically.

name: v0.13.0-dev01
body:
First dev pre-release of the 0.13.0 minor, retargeted from 0.12.1 (what accumulated across dev01-dev04 there was genuinely new functionality, not patch-level fixes, so the version number is being corrected here). If you've been on the Dev channel already, you've seen the dev01-dev04 content below, new this round is the Fixed section's first six entries.

### Fixed (new since dev04)
- Radio's volume control no longer overflows off-screen; redesigned as a single continuous pill that flows straight out of the volume icon.
- Radio now auto-reconnects at the live edge after a dropped connection, instead of resuming stale buffered audio or getting stuck.
- The desktop fullscreen title bar no longer reappears if an episode auto-advances to the next one while fullscreen.
- The Up Next card's Play Now/Hide buttons no longer overflow.
- SyncPlay's group row no longer overflows with a long group name or a longer translated label.
- Seerr's request dialogs no longer overflow their Cancel/Save/Request buttons in some translations (German among them).

### Also in this release
Carried over from dev01-dev04, already covered in their own notes if you saw those: Watchlist, radio station-skip controls, unified right-click/long-press menus everywhere, YouTube Downloads multi-select, a Windows installer, real ffmpeg for Android YouTube downloads, the YouTube downloads floating pill, a Download Location setting, plus earlier fixes for context-menu positioning, download slowdowns, downloaded-YouTube playback parity, the Now Playing volume/keyboard-inset bugs, the What's New tab rate-limit issue, the no-keyring startup crash, and the Seerr API-key request bug.

Tester build, report anything odd. The in-app updater's Dev channel will offer this build automatically.

name: v0.12.1-dev04
body:
Fourth dev pre-release of the 0.12.1 patch.

### Added
- Watchlist: a Netflix-style "want to watch" list, separate from Favorites. Toggle it from the detail page's bookmark icon or an item's context menu; find it from the Libraries browse bar, or add it to the main nav from Settings > Navigation. Backed by a hidden per-account Jellyfin playlist, so it syncs across your devices like Favorites already does.
- Radio gets real previous/next-station controls: on the Android notification, Android Auto, Linux/Windows media controls, and directly on the radio Now Playing screen. Cycles through your saved stations in the same order the Radio screen shows them (Favorites, then each group, then Ungrouped). (#41, thanks @Epic-dog)
- Right-click and long-press now open the same menu as the "..." button everywhere in the app: Downloads, Radio station rows, Album tracks, and the Seerr Requests tab (previously only Jellyfin library items had this).
- YouTube Downloads: multi-select and bulk delete. Long-press a finished download, or use Select from its own menu.
- A Windows installer alongside the existing portable zip, with a proper Start Menu entry and uninstaller. (#43, thanks @Epic-dog)

### Changed
- Right-click/long-press menus now look and behave identically everywhere: a small dropdown at the pointer on a mouse-driven desktop, a bottom sheet on touch/TV, instead of Jellyfin and YouTube each rolling their own look.
- "Add Favorite"/"Remove Favorite" reworded to "Add to Favorites"/"Remove from Favorites", matching Watchlist's wording.
- The YouTube download-complete notification now opens the YouTube Downloads tab instead of the Jellyfin downloads screen.

### Fixed
- Right-click/long-press context menus no longer open away from the item they're for.
- A slowdown when several YouTube downloads run at once.
- Downloaded YouTube video playback now supports Next (through other completed downloads), minimize/PiP, and captions/SponsorBlock, matching what watching online already does.

Tester build, report anything odd. New this round especially: Watchlist, radio station-skip, and the Windows installer. The in-app updater's Dev channel will offer this build automatically.

name: v0.12.1-dev03
body:
Third dev pre-release of the 0.12.1 patch.

### Added
- Android YouTube downloads now go through a real ffmpeg, matching desktop: higher-than-360p video, MKV, and MP3 audio all work instead of being permanently capped at 360p MP4 / M4A. (#46, thanks @urtaevS)
- A floating progress pill for YouTube downloads too, matching the one Jellyfin downloads already had. Both stack instead of overlapping when active at the same time.

### Fixed
- The volume icon on the Now Playing screen no longer overlaps the repeat button, and the whole control cluster now scales down gracefully on narrow phones instead of overlapping or clipping.
- The Now Playing screen (music, radio, and YouTube audio) no longer goes blank below the seek bar after a stuck keyboard inset — none of these screens have a text field, so they no longer react to one. (#40, thanks @urtaevS)
- Downloaded YouTube videos now resume where you left off and show the channel name/art on the lock screen, matching what watching online already does — they'd been playing through a bare, minimal player with neither.

Tester build, report anything odd. Android downloads especially: please try a higher-than-360p video and an MP3 audio download and let me know if anything fails. The in-app updater's Dev channel will offer future dev builds automatically.

name: v0.12.1-dev02
body:
Second dev pre-release of the 0.12.1 patch.

### Added
- A Download Location setting (General > Storage) for downloaded Jellyfin media, movies, TV shows, music, and recordings, separate from the existing YouTube video/audio folders. Files are organized into Movies/TV Shows/Music/Recordings subfolders. Defaults to app-private storage.

### Fixed
- The What's New YouTube tab no longer spins for minutes or comes back empty. It was fetching an exact upload date for every video individually to sort the feed, which could trip YouTube's rate limiter with a large subscription list; it now sorts using the relative date YouTube already provides, with no extra network calls. (#38, thanks @jtbrauer92-p)

### Changed
- The Shortcuts settings row (rebindable keyboard shortcuts) no longer shows on phones and tablets, where there's no hardware keyboard to bind.

Tester build, report anything odd. The in-app updater's Dev channel will offer future dev builds automatically.

name: v0.12.1-dev01
body:
First dev pre-release of the 0.12.1 patch.

### Fixed
- Fathom no longer crashes on startup in environments with no system keyring at all, such as Steam Big Picture / gamescope on Linux. It now falls back to a local unencrypted store automatically when this happens, which also fixes login, saved passwords, downloads, and other settings in these environments. (#32, thanks @tangowithfoxtrot)
- Requesting media through Seerr while signed in with your Jellyfin username and password no longer fails with an API key error. The request dialog no longer shows a "Request As" option for a Jellyfin/local sign-in (that's an admin-only feature), and the request is correctly attributed to you automatically.

name: v0.12.0
body:
Fathom 0.12.0 turns Downloads into a full offline library, adds self-service password changes, and fixes YouTube's bot-gate and dubbed-audio playback issues.

## Added
- Downloads is now a full offline library, organized into Movies, TV Shows, Recordings, and Music sections with the same poster covers and rating badges as your regular library. (#29)
- Opening a downloaded title shows the same detail page as its library page (backdrop, cast, ratings, overview), scoped to what's downloaded: only the episodes you have, with local-only Play, Mark Watched, and Remove that never touch your Jellyfin server.
- Download a whole series or season in one go, picking a scope (all episodes or a single season); every episode also has its own download option in its menu, and a floating pill shows progress with a Cancel All action. (#27)
- Download music, a single track or a whole album/artist; it plays in the music player with the familiar album view, and works fully offline.
- Download Live TV recordings; they land in their own Recordings section.
- Change your own password from the Profile screen (current password, new password, confirm). Leaving the new password blank removes it, the same "no password" option the official Jellyfin clients offer.
- Update checks now have a frequency setting (on/off, plus Every Launch, Daily, or Weekly) on the Updates screen.
- Shuffle and repeat for background YouTube audio, plus skip back to the previous track.
- Nix flake for Linux, so you can build and run Fathom with `nix build` / `nix run`. (thanks @numkem)

## Changed
- In a series, tapping an episode row opens its page. Tap the thumbnail or the play icon to play the episode directly. (#20, thanks @numkem)
- YouTube live streams start in a couple of seconds instead of tens of seconds.
- The Cast button reads "Cast" instead of "Cast to."
- A new build is now announced with a redesigned floating banner and a native system notification on Linux and Android, instead of a passing in-app message.

## Fixed
- YouTube playback works again. Audio and video had been blocked by YouTube's "confirm you're not a bot" gate. Fathom now resolves streams through the VISIONOS client, which plays without it.
- YouTube videos with multiple audio languages no longer default to a dubbed track. Fathom now picks the default (English) audio track instead of whichever has the highest bitrate. (#30, thanks @shiftyfox380)
- Background YouTube audio no longer freezes on an unplayable track, and recovers from brief network drops instead of stalling on the next song.
- Saved radio stations are no longer left out of settings backups.
- Importing YouTube subscriptions on Android no longer greys out files from cloud storage providers like Drive, Nextcloud, and Proton. (#23)
- The desktop window buttons (minimize, maximize, close) now hide when the YouTube player goes fullscreen on Windows and Linux.
- Detail page action buttons expand on touch on Android again.
- On Linux, settings and your Jellyfin login now persist on minimal desktops where the system keyring starts cold, such as Hyprland sessions. The app no longer returns to the setup screen on every launch. (#25, thanks @joejosephs)
- In-app updates on Android work again. A change in how builds were numbered had Android rejecting a newer build as a downgrade, so the update failed part way through. Builds are now always numbered above the last, so updates install.
- Duplicate "Fathom" launcher icons on Linux, when running the AppImage on GNOME, no longer appear. Fathom manages its own launcher entry and now tells AppImage integrators to stand down. (#28)

## Install
- Linux: `Fathom-x86_64.AppImage` (or `Fathom-aarch64.AppImage`), `chmod +x` and run.
- Windows: `Fathom-windows-x64.zip`, unzip and run `fathom.exe`.
- Android (phones, tablets, and experimental Android TV): `Fathom-0.12.0.apk`.

body:
Sixth dev pre-release of the 0.12.0 minor. A big Downloads pass: a proper offline library, downloaded music that plays in the music player, and Live TV recordings that download into their own section.

### Added
- Downloads is now a full offline library (#29), organized into Movies, Music, Recordings, and TV Shows, each a poster grid that behaves just like the main library, same cover size, rating badges, and unwatched counts.
- A downloaded title opens a detail page identical to its library page (backdrop, poster, cast and crew, every enabled rating, overview, genres), but scoped to the download folder: only the episodes you have, and every action stays local to Downloads.
- Download music: a single track, or a whole album or artist (which queues its tracks). Downloaded music plays in the music player with the familiar album view, blurred cover backdrop, album art in the mini and full player, track durations, and an animated now-playing indicator, and it all works offline.
- Download Live TV recordings. They download into their own Recordings section, whether you grab a whole recorded series or a single episode.
- A download-only "Mark Watched" that never touches your server, plus a per-episode menu (Play, Mark Watched, Remove download).
- When you download a series, pick a scope: everything, or a single season. (#27)
- A dismissible banner when a new build is available, with a shortcut to the Updates screen, and a system notification for it on Android.

### Changed
- The Downloads queue shows a floating pill (tap it to open Downloads) with a Cancel All action, and a series' episodes group by season with per-season cancel.
- Cover art, backdrops, cast photos, and episode thumbnails are cached at download time, so a downloaded detail page renders fully offline (episodes show their stills, matching the server view). Extra online ratings (Rotten Tomatoes, Letterboxd, and the rest) are cached too, and refresh whenever you open the page online.
- On a downloaded page, Cast and "Play on another device" appear only when they can actually work (online, with a target), since both stream from the server.

name: Dev Build (latest)
body:
Fourth dev pre-release of the 0.13.1 patch.

### Added
- **Settings, Support:** a new page with Ko-fi, GitHub Sponsors and free ways to help.

### Changed
- **Downloads** from your Jellyfin server are saved under readable names with their real file extension, such as `Bullet Train (2022).mkv` or `Show - S01E02 - Episode.mp4`, so other apps and file managers recognise them. Downloads you already have keep their current names.
- **Diagnostics** now include the media commands Android delivers to Fathom (from the notification, lock screen, earbuds and headsets) and changes in audio focus, to pin down controls that stop responding.

### Fixed
- **Android:** notification, lock screen and earbud controls could stop responding after you stopped playback in Fathom and started it again. Fathom now stays connected to them.
- **Android:** after another app has played audio, pressing play in Fathom takes the audio back, so disconnecting your earbuds pauses it again and two apps no longer play over each other.

Tester build, report anything odd. New this round especially: media controls after stopping and restarting playback, or after listening in another app; and the names of new downloads. If the controls stop responding, copy the Diagnostics report: its new Android media commands section shows where each press went. The in-app updater's Dev channel will offer this build automatically.

Fathom is free and always will be. Support on [Ko-fi](https://ko-fi.com/traceapps) goes toward a Mac and an iPhone so my apps can come to Apple devices, and [GitHub Sponsors](https://github.com/sponsors/TraceApps?metadata_app=fathom&metadata_from=release) helps with the monthly costs.

name: v0.11.0
body:
Fathom 0.11.0 brings the app to Android and Android TV, adds a YouTube Shorts viewer, Android Auto, and an Up Next prompt, and lets you manage and delete items in place.

> Note: Android TV support is experimental in this release and still being refined. Android phones and tablets, and the Linux and Windows desktop apps, are the stable targets.

## Added
- Android, and experimental Android TV: Fathom now runs on Android phones and tablets from the same universal APK, at parity with the desktop player (skip, trickplay, picture-in-picture, SyncPlay), with Chromecast and background YouTube audio with lock-screen controls. A native ExoPlayer backend is the default on Android TV (and optional on phones) for tunneled 4K/HDR playback. Android TV is included but experimental: D-pad navigation and a 10-foot interface are in place, with more polish to come.
- Android Auto (audio-only): browse your Jellyfin music, internet radio, and YouTube in tabs, search by voice, and control playback, shuffle, repeat, favorites, and the up-next queue from the car's screen.
- YouTube Shorts viewer: a vertical swipe pager through a channel's Shorts, with comments, a scrubbable progress bar, watch history, and portrait fullscreen.
- Up Next: episodes that have a next episode show an Up Next prompt over the credits, as a poster Card or a Netflix-style Pill, so it advances to the next episode instead of leaving you at the end of the file. Choose the style and timing under Settings, and Autoplay Next Episode decides whether it counts down on its own or waits for Play Now.
- Item context menu: a per-item menu on posters (long-press, right-click, or the hover hamburger), on each episode row, and in the detail overflow, with Play or Resume, Show Details, Mark Watched, Add to Favorites, Add to Playlist, Refresh Metadata, and Delete.
- Delete media: with the right server permission, delete a whole series, a season, a single episode, or a movie, each behind a confirmation.
- Audio passthrough: bitstream Atmos, Dolby Digital, and DTS to a receiver on the desktop player.
- Skip Recap: "Previously On" recaps get their own Skip Recap button, separate from Skip Intro.

## Changed
- Plugin configuration is now an in-app form (toggles, number and text fields, add/remove lists) instead of a raw JSON blob, with an Edit as JSON switch, plus plugin logos in the list and on the plugin page.
- Faster YouTube "What's New" and channel browsing (InnerTube, bounded hydration, cached feed metadata).
- YouTube audio now uses higher-resolution artwork.
- Your last volume is restored when playback hands off between the player and background audio.

## Fixed
- Skip Intro and Skip Credits now appear reliably (the app requests segment types from the server).
- Desktop fullscreen: the window's minimize, maximize, and close buttons are now hidden, and Space and the other player shortcuts work in fullscreen as well as windowed.
- Seerr search no longer fails on multi-word queries.

## Install
- Linux: `Fathom-x86_64.AppImage` (or `Fathom-aarch64.AppImage`), `chmod +x` and run.
- Windows: `Fathom-windows-x64.zip`, unzip and run `fathom.exe`.
- Android (phones, tablets, and experimental Android TV): `Fathom-0.11.0.apk`.

Dev build from the `dev` branch (heading toward 0.11.0). Not a stable release.

Changes since v0.11.0-dev02:

- **Item Menu:** New per-item context menu, the same idea as the one in Jellyfin and Fladder. Long-press a poster, right-click it, or hover and use the hamburger in the bottom corner to Play or Resume, Show Details, mark watched, add to favorites, add to a playlist, refresh metadata, or delete. The item menu is reachable on TV from an episode's three-dot button and from the detail overflow.

name: v0.11.0-dev02
body:
Dev build from the `dev` branch (heading toward 0.11.0). Not a stable release.

Changes since v0.11.0-dev01:

- **Android Auto:** New audio-only Android Auto support. Browse your Jellyfin music, internet radio, and YouTube in tabs, search (including by voice) to play a song or playlist, and control playback, shuffle, repeat, favorites, and the up-next queue from the car's screen.
- **Up Next:** Episodes that have a next episode now show an Up Next prompt over the credits instead of a plain Skip Credits button, so it takes you to the next episode rather than to the end of the file. Choose a poster Card or a compact Netflix-style Pill under Settings > Playback, set how long it stays before auto-skipping (the whole credits, or a short countdown of 30, 20, 15, 10, or 5 seconds), and Autoplay Next Episode decides whether it counts down on its own or just waits for you to press Play Now.
- **Skip Buttons:** Skip Intro and Skip Credits now appear reliably (the app asks the server for segment types), "Previously On" recaps get their own Skip Recap button separate from Skip Intro, and the skip and Up Next prompts fade in instead of popping.
- **Plugins:** Plugin configuration is now an in-app form with real toggles, number and text fields, and add/remove lists instead of a raw JSON blob, with an Edit as JSON switch if you prefer the raw view. Plugin logos also appear in the plugins list and on the plugin page.
- **YouTube:** On Android TV, Shorts are shown as a 9:16 column with a blurred backdrop instead of being stretched widescreen, and the lighter right-edge strip is gone. The TV player gains a YouTube actions sheet (Subscribe, Add to Playlist, open Channel), YouTube audio uses higher-resolution artwork, and the Listen queue no longer gets stuck when a track fails to open.
- **Audio:** New audio passthrough setting to bitstream Atmos, Dolby Digital, and DTS to a receiver on the desktop player, and your last volume is restored when playback hands off between the player and background audio.
- **Android TV:** The skip buttons and the new Up Next prompt work on the TV player, with D-pad focus and larger sizing for the 10-foot view, plus focus rings added across more screens.
- **Android (ExoPlayer):** 4:3 video is no longer stretched to fill a 16:9 screen (it pillarboxes now, matching the desktop player), and seeking near the end of an episode no longer jumps you to the next one.
- **Casting:** The cast button now fades away with the rest of the player controls instead of floating over the video after they hide.
- **Now Playing:** Switching from YouTube audio to internet radio or music now updates the OS media controls and Android Auto with the correct title, artwork, and time instead of keeping the previous YouTube track's info.

Tester build, report anything odd. The in-app updater's Dev channel will offer future dev builds automatically.
